candidate.answerReason: Integer points on the line have coordinates (1+11k,1+111k) for integer k. Strictly between the endpoints requires 0<k<9, giving eight possibilities.

methods.label: Use the line equation and divisibility
methods.explanation:
The slope tells us when an integer horizontal step also produces an integer vertical step. Since the horizontal difference between the endpoints is \(99\ne0\), the line has slope
\[\frac{1000-1}{100-1}=\frac{999}{99}=\frac{111}{11}.\]
Using \(A(1,1)\), its equation is
\[y-1=\frac{111}{11}(x-1)=10(x-1)+\frac{x-1}{11}.\]
For an integer \(x\), the term \(10(x-1)\) is already an integer. Therefore \(y\) is an integer exactly when \(x-1\) is divisible by \(11\). Write \(x=1+11k\), where \(k\) is an integer; then \(y=1+111k\).

Strictly between the endpoints means \(1<x<100\), so
\[0<11k<99,\qquad 0<k<9.\]
Thus \(k=1,2,\ldots,8\). Each gives a distinct point on the segment, and the divisibility argument includes every integer-coordinate point. There are \(8\) such points, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
